effects.description: A burst at 0/30/80 ms saves only latest text at 200 ms after maintenance; immediate baseline saves every edit.
A later burst receives its own complete quiet interval and saves after the first batch retired.
Close at 20 ms commits document-owned text before return after retiring its badge; no stale timer repeats it.
Switch before the first deadline saves A before return and never retargets its pending text into B.
Close and reopen the same document before the deadline restore latest text without retaining an old batch.
A pending flush notifies inline and opens C inside outer open B; the newer navigation survives outer return. The immediate baseline already notified before the callback was armed.
A pending flush notifies inline and closes inside outer open B; outer navigation must not reopen it. The immediate baseline has no pending notification.
A timer-fired save opens B through inline notification; the detached A badge is skipped and B subsequently saves with an active badge.
An inline notification edits the still-active document again; the new burst survives retirement of the first batch.
Preview emits exactly once at either its original 40 ms quiet interval or the separately authorized 120 ms interval.
Hiding a preview discards pending query work and never flushes it in either authorization arm.
A hidden then reused preview publishes only its new query with the same quiet interval as an uninterrupted preview.
Preview has one coherent 40 ms or authorized 120 ms policy, preserves reuse, and always discards hidden work.
The adjacent preview quiet interval is changed to 120 ms; this scope extension requires explicit authorization.
Submit an active pending edit at 20 ms; verify store at archive capture and return, immutable receipt, live notice, and no duplicate save.
The same submission occurs after the quiet save, requiring no duplicate commit.
Arm save callback after edit, submit while pending, callback opens C: keep A receipt but suppress A notice; then submit C successfully.
The pending submit save closes the editor inline: keep and return A receipt with no visible notice.
Save callback closes then reopens A: same document key must not revive the old visit notice; later new-visit submit remains live.
During a pending submit save, callback edits the same visit: the receipt retains entry text and the subsequent batch saves on its own deadline.
Submission with no active document returns null, archives nothing, and schedules no work.
Dispose detaches integration before pending departure commit and keeps closed actions inert.
Empty string is valid pending text; two accepts make two receipts but do not duplicate the save.
Large Unicode/newline text survives the native value handoff; subsequent edits cannot change receipt values.
